summary: MODEL_CHANGE_REQUIRED: the update moves the learner's hand-off of synced proposals before the NEWLEADER ACK. The model, Trace spec and harness were updated and validated; model checking found that the ACK still precedes durability (MC-1, reproduced on the update and the old revision), and code review found three update-introduced sync/lifecycle defects (CR-1..CR-3, reproduced).
validation_limits: All model checking is bounded (3 servers, 1 txn, up to 3 epochs, 2 crashes, 1 drop/snapshot); BFS runs stopped at 30-minute budgets with non-empty queues, so no-violation results are LIMITED_COVERAGE, not proofs.

The deep U2/U3 witnesses (depth 25/38 from Init) were not reached by BFS or simulation from Init; they were found from a seed state that full MCNext reaches from Init (canary-seed.log) and re-found with full MCNext from that seed.
Open/discharge checking is not applicable: Update.tla defines no EnvUpdate; focused relations are restrictions of MCNext.

Not modeled: late joiners to a broadcasting leader, observers, reconfiguration, exception/liveness paths (handled by code review CR-1..CR-3); zxid order approximated by log length; FLE votes persist across rounds; TRUNC does not roll back the visible committed/applied state.
Fresh traces did not exercise SyncProposalApplied, the TRUNC directive, or a crash inside the ACK-to-fsync window (the reproduction test covers the crash window).
Known-status (issue/history) searches for the findings were not performed because the run is blind; novelty is undetermined.
Only JDK 21 was available; the hypothetical flush-before-ACK control is a local patch, not an upstream fix.

findings.title: NEWLEADER ACK is sent before the DIFF-synchronized history is durable
findings.cause: Learner.syncWithLeader hands buffered proposals to FollowerZooKeeperServer.logRequest, which only enqueues to SyncRequestProcessor, and writes the NEWLEADER ACK without waiting for append/fsync; currentEpoch is already persisted.
findings.trigger: A leader with an uncommitted logged txn is re-elected; a follower DIFF-syncs it, ACKs NEWLEADER (counted toward the quorum, leader serves the txn) and crashes before SyncThread forces the log; it restarts with the new epoch and, with another server lacking the txn, elects a new leader.
findings.consequence: A transaction the previous leader already served after its NEWLEADER quorum is missing at the next leader (lost or truncated cluster-wide).

premises: The NEWLEADER ACK is written without waiting for the SyncRequestProcessor flush of the handed-off proposals.
The leader counts that ACK toward its NEWLEADER quorum and then serves its initial history.
Fail-stop crashes lose appended-but-unforced log records; currentEpoch is persisted before the ACK.

findings.title: COMMIT between NEWLEADER and UPTODATE dereferences an empty packetsNotCommitted (NPE)
findings.cause: The update clears packetsNotCommitted at NEWLEADER; the COMMIT branch dereferences packetsNotCommitted.peekFirst() without a null check.
findings.trigger: The leader forwards a PROPOSAL before NEWLEADER (startForwarding precedes NEWLEADER) and its COMMIT after NEWLEADER but before UPTODATE.
findings.consequence: NullPointerException in Learner.syncWithLeader; the learner abandons synchronization and cannot join until a retry avoids the interleaving.

premises: A COMMIT for a proposal forwarded before NEWLEADER can arrive before UPTODATE.

findings.title: Request processors started at NEWLEADER are not shut down when synchronization fails before UPTODATE
findings.cause: startupWithoutServing starts the processors but leaves state INITIAL; LearnerZooKeeperServer.shutdown returns early because canShutdown() is false.
findings.trigger: Any learner failure between NEWLEADER and startServing (e.g. CR-1 or the read timeout injected by DIFFSyncConsistencyTest).
findings.consequence: Leaked FollowerRequestProcessor/CommitProcessor/RequestThrottler threads; the orphaned SyncThread keeps flushing and dies with a critical-thread error writing to the closed learner socket.

premises: A learner can fail after NEWLEADER and before startServing.

findings.title: A SyncThread per-txn ACK can overtake the NEWLEADER ACK
findings.cause: The update starts SyncRequestProcessor/SendAckRequestProcessor and hands off txns before the learner thread writes the NEWLEADER ACK; LearnerHandler treats the first ACK after NEWLEADER as the NEWLEADER ACK.
findings.trigger: The learner thread is delayed longer than one append+fsync between logRequest and writing the NEWLEADER ACK.
findings.consequence: Leader.waitForNewLeaderAck rejects the ACK as from a different epoch and the real NEWLEADER ACK is ignored; the leader does not form its NEWLEADER quorum and stalls until the init limit.

premises: SyncThread can write a per-txn ACK before the learner thread writes the NEWLEADER ACK.
